document_name: Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States, 221 U.S. 1 (1911) .pdf
brief_summary: This document is the official Supreme Court opinion for the landmark case *Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States*, decided in 1911. It primarily concerns the interpretation of the Sherman Anti-trust Act of 1890. The Court establishes the influential "Rule of Reason," holding that the Act prohibits only *unreasonable* or *undue* restraints of trade. Applying this standard, the Court found Standard Oil's combination to be an unreasonable restraint on interstate commerce in petroleum and its products.
